threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP vision, target users, and success metrics for the feedback hub.

messages.text: Hello team! Kicking off the Data-Driven Feedback Hub project. I've created a draft of the vision, target users, and success metrics in A1. This covers the first big task, T1. Please take a look and share your feedback here by EOD tomorrow.
Thanks for getting this started. The vision statement is clear. On the personas in A1, is the 'Sales Manager' a primary or secondary user for the MVP? Just want to ensure we're focused.
This looks good. A quick question to make sure I understand, when we say 'user' are we talking about the sales reps who input the feedback, or the product team who reads it?

Good question. For the MVP, the Sales Rep is the primary user persona, focused on quickly logging feedback. The Sales Manager is secondary, mainly for viewing team feedback. It's detailed on page 2 of A1.
Both are users, but for the MVP scope, our primary persona is the internal user who needs to *access* the consolidated feedback, so Product, Sales, and Support leads. The doc A1 has the breakdown.
Ah, okay, that clarifies it. Thanks.

The proposed success metrics look solid. Metric #3, 'Time to Insight', might be hard to quantify automatically with our current tools. For the pilot, we might need to rely on a qualitative user survey to measure that one.

We could also add a metric around 'Training Effectiveness Score'. I can quickly build a quiz that pilot users take after the enablement session to measure comprehension of the hub's purpose and features.
That's a fair point on 'Time to Insight'. A survey is a good, lightweight solution for the pilot. Let's go with that.

Appreciate the proactive thinking! While that's a great idea for a more mature program, let's keep the pilot's success metrics tightly focused on the tool's adoption and impact itself. We can add training effectiveness to the V2 backlog.
Understood, makes sense to keep it focused for now.

Okay, great discussion everyone. It sounds like we have alignment. Let's formalize the decisions. D1: The MVP vision and primary user personas (Sales Reps, Product Managers) as defined in A1 are approved.
And D2: The initial success metrics for the pilot are: 1. Weekly Active Users (WAU) of the hub, 2. Number of feedback items tagged per week, and 3. User Satisfaction Score (via a post-pilot survey).
Looks good. This gives us a clear direction.
Metrics are clear and measurable. I can start thinking about the data sources for these.
Perfect. I will update A1 to reflect these decisions. Next up is T2, mapping the current feedback flows.

threads.thread_goal: Lock MVP scope by agreeing on data sources and core workflows.

messages.text: Hi team, as a follow-up to T2, I've mapped the current feedback flows and inventoried the data sources in A2. Based on this, I've proposed a list of data sources and core workflows for the MVP. Please review and share your thoughts.

Thanks for putting this together so quickly. The map in A2 is very clear. I see 'Sales Call Notes from CRM' is listed as a source. Given the ongoing CRM upgrade, relying on its API is a project risk. For the MVP, I propose we limit scope to 'Support Tickets (Zendesk)' and 'NPS Survey Comments (Qualtrics)' which have stable, well-documented APIs.
What about the feedback that our sales reps get in emails? Can we connect to their inboxes to pull that data too? It seems like a rich source of information.

That's a great point, but parsing unstructured emails is technically complex and raises data privacy concerns. One of our project constraints is to use existing internal tools with structured data. Let's add 'unstructured email parsing' to our future roadmap ideas but keep it out of the MVP scope to avoid data quality issues.
Okay, understood. Sticking to structured sources makes sense. I will focus on the data model for Zendesk and Qualtrics for T4 then.
Regarding workflows, the document mentions viewing and filtering. What about the triage process outlined in A3? Will users be able to assign feedback or change its status directly in the hub?

For the MVP, the hub is primarily a single source of truth for viewing insights. The triage and prioritization process (T7) will be a manual, weekly meeting run by the product team, using the hub's dashboard as the primary input. We want to validate the governance model in A3 before we build workflow automation around it.
Got it. View-only first, action later. That simplifies the user journey significantly.
Okay, I'll update the requirements doc to reflect these decisions. So to summarize for everyone...
Exactly. Let's lock it in. Decision D3: The data sources in scope for the MVP are Support Tickets (Zendesk) and NPS Survey Comments (Qualtrics). All other sources are out of scope.

And decision D4: The core user workflows for the first release are: 1. View consolidated feedback on a dashboard, 2. Filter feedback by data source, date, and product line, and 3. Apply predefined tags to feedback items. No in-tool assignment or status changes.
Confirmed. I'll finalize the requirements for T4 based on this. Thanks everyone.

threads.thread_goal: Review and iterate on user journeys, UX wireframes, and training approach.

messages.text: Hi all, I've created the first draft of the low-fidelity UX wireframes based on our agreed workflows. You can find them in A4. This is the first pass at T3, looking forward to your feedback.

And I've drafted a comprehensive training plan to cover T6 and T9! See the draft of A5. It includes a 3-part webinar series, pre-reading materials, and post-session knowledge checks. I also started a draft of the data privacy guide A7 as part of T12.

Thanks both. Reviewing A4 now. The dashboard layout is clean. One suggestion: on the main feedback view, could we make the filter panel collapsible? It takes up a lot of real estate, and users might only set filters once per session.
That's a great idea, it would make the view much cleaner. Easy change to make. I'll update the wireframe.
The user journey looks logical. A question on compliance: where do we remind users about the data privacy rules from A7? Should we add a link to the guide in the footer of the application?
Yes, good catch. A link in the footer to the A7 'Acceptable Use Reference' is a simple and effective way to handle that. I'll add it to the design.

@156956 This is an incredibly thorough training plan in A5. To minimize friction for the pilot and avoid the risk of low adoption, I'd suggest we scale it back. Let's do a single, 30-minute live demo session that's very hands-on. We can offer your detailed deck as an optional, self-service resource for users who want to learn more.

Okay, I can see that. A single session would be easier to schedule and get attendance for. I'll rework the materials to fit a 30-minute interactive demo for T9 and position the A5 deck as a quick-start guide.

Perfect. With those adjustments, I think we're ready to approve these. D5: The UX for the main user journeys in A4 is approved, with the changes for a collapsible filter panel and a footer link to A7.
And D6: The training format for pilot participants will be a single 30-minute live demo, supported by the A5 quick-start guide as a leave-behind resource.
Great, I'll finalize the T3 wireframes today.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize pilot rollout plan, measurement framework, and governance.

messages.text: Morning team. I've drafted the pilot rollout plan for T5, which details the target user groups, timeline, and communication strategy. It's ready for your review.
To go along with that, I've set up the Pilot Measurement and KPI Tracker in A6. This aligns with the metrics from A1 and will be our source of truth for T10.
The plan for T5 looks solid. The timeline is ambitious but achievable. For the communication plan, have we decided on the cadence for updating stakeholders outside this core team?
Good question. I've planned for a weekly summary email that includes a snapshot of the A6 dashboard. I'll make that more explicit in the document.
I'm looking at the governance model in A3 again. For the pilot, will users need a way to escalate or assign feedback within the tool itself? Or is that handled outside the hub?

That's an important clarification. The governance process for T7 is manual for the pilot. The triage committee will meet weekly to review the hub's dashboard and make decisions offline. We want to test the process before we build software to support it.
Okay, that makes sense. Manual process first. Thanks for clarifying.
The manual triage process is documented in the A3 playbook, so we can point users there if they have questions.

Alright, seems we have consensus. Let's finalize these decisions so we can move forward. D7: The pilot scope, target groups (NA Sales & Support), and 3-week timeline as defined in the T5 doc are confirmed.
And D8: The KPIs and reporting cadence in A6 are approved. The triage governance for the pilot will follow the manual process documented in A3.
All clear. Ready for rollout.

threads.thread_goal: Synthesize pilot results and align on next-phase roadmap.

messages.text: Team, the pilot has officially wrapped up! A huge thank you for all your hard work. I've consolidated the key results, learnings, and user feedback in the summary doc A8. The final pilot metrics are also updated in A6.

Based on the findings, I've drafted some high-level roadmap options for our next phase as part of T11, which you can find at the end of A8. The main options are: 1) Expand to the EMEA region, 2) Integrate a new data source (e.g., App Store reviews), or 3) Build out the in-tool triage workflow. I'm leaning towards option 2 for the biggest impact.

This is a great summary. The usage metrics in A6 exceeded our targets. One qualitative learning I'd add is that we saw some inconsistency in how users applied tags. For the next phase, we should consider refining the tagging taxonomy or providing better descriptions.

The feedback on the training session was also fantastic! I collected some great quotes. Users loved the 30-minute format. A few people mentioned that the calendar invite was sent out a bit late, so we can improve that next time. Someone also asked about having recurring 'office hours'.
Excellent point on the taxonomy. That's a critical data quality improvement we need to prioritize regardless of which roadmap option we choose. I'll add it to A8.
Thanks for gathering that! All good operational feedback for our next rollout.

The roadmap options in A8 are well-reasoned. I agree that integrating a new data source probably delivers the most value right now. I suggest we schedule a meeting with our key stakeholders to walk them through A8 and get their formal buy-in on the T11 roadmap.
A meeting sounds good. Having the data from A6 will make for a strong business case.

Agreed. I'll find time on the calendar for this week and send out an invite with A8 as a pre-read. The goal will be to leave that meeting with a firm decision on the next phase. Thanks again everyone for a successful pilot!
